prompt: My landlord is deducting ₹10,000 for painting.
raw_response:
I understand how frustrating it is when a landlord makes unfair deductions from your hard-earned security deposit.

### | Your Situation
You are a tenant in India whose landlord has arbitrarily deducted ₹10,000 from your security deposit specifically for painting charges. The core issue is whether such deductions are permissible under Indian tenancy laws for normal usage of the property.

### | Your Legal Position
- Under Section 108(m) and (o) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a tenant is bound to restore the property in as good condition as it was at the start of the tenancy, subject only to reasonable wear and tear.
- "Reasonable wear and tear" refers to the natural and gradual deterioration of a property due to normal day-to-day use over time, for which a tenant cannot be held financially liable.
- Under the Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (and applicable state tenancy laws), a landlord is required to refund the security deposit upon taking over vacant possession, minus only valid deductions expressly agreed upon in the tenancy agreement or for damage caused beyond normal wear and tear.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence: Collect your signed tenancy agreement, photographs or videos showing the condition of the apartment when you moved out, and the written communication or receipt showing the arbitrary deduction of ₹10,000.
2. Send a written demand notice granting 15 days: Issue a formal legal notice to your landlord demanding the immediate refund of the ₹10,000 deduction, explaining that painting due to normal aging falls under reasonable wear and tear.
3. Appropriate forum: If the landlord fails to refund the amount within 15 days, approach the local Rent Authority or file a summary suit before the appropriate civil court for recovery of the withheld security deposit.

### Information I still need from you
Did you have a written tenancy agreement, and did it explicitly state that you are required to pay for painting upon vacating the premises?

citations.description: Lessee is bound to keep and restore the property in as good condition as it was at the time he was put in possession, subject only to reasonable wear and tear and irresistible force. Landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage painting without explicit contractual basis.

citations.title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
citations.description: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for other than agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be month-to-month, terminable on 15 days' notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.

citations.title: Cap on Security Deposit and Condition for Deductions
citations.description: Limits security deposit for residential premises to a maximum of two months' rent. Requires refund of security deposit to the tenant at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making valid deductions agreed under the tenancy agreement.
citations.jurisdiction: Model Central Act (Adopted by States such as AP, TN, UP)

citations.title: Suit by person dispossessed of immovable property without due process
citations.description: If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immovable property otherwise than in due course of law, he or any person claiming through him may, by suit, recover possession thereof notwithstanding any other title that may be set up.
